protocol.title: Continuous-Flow Biomolecule and Cell Concentrator by Ion Concentration Polarization
protocol.platform: Nanofluidic PDMS microfluidic chip with Nafion nanojunction (cation-selective membrane)
targets: FITC-lectin from Lens culinaris (positively and negatively charged protein)
protocol.objective: Continuous-flow preconcentration of charged biomolecules and cells using ICP (ion concentration polarization) at a Nafion nanojunction; concentration factors from 1 to ~200 achieved by adjusting channel geometry (width ratio w' and length ratio l')

device.material: PDMS (poly(dimethylsiloxane)) bonded to Nafion-patterned glass substrate by plasma treatment
device.fabrication: Standard soft lithography; PDMS molds for Nafion nanojunction and microchannels by photolithography

nafion.type: Nafion perfluorinated ion-exchange resin, 20 wt% solution (Sigma-Aldrich)
nafion.selectivity: Cation-selective; sulfonate groups provide nanometer-scale ion pathways
nafion.patterning: PDMS line mold (width 100 um, height 50 um) on clean glass substrate
nafion.orientation: Parallel to and along the concentrated channel

main_channel.note: Width varied across devices; bifurcates into concentrated and filtered channels

concentrated_channel.note: Fixed at 20 um for most experiments; 10 um for FITC-lectin high-factor tests

filtered_channel.note: w' = (w1+w2)/w1; l' = L1/L2; both control concentration factor r

channels.buffer_channel: Ground electrode channel; electrical ground for ICP voltage application

concentration_factor.range: 1 to ~200 (theoretical); experimental always lower than theoretical due to ICP-induced flow velocity changes
concentration_factor.note: Concentration factor is target-independent; same geometry gives same factor for any charged species

voltage_V.note: 150 V/cm ~ 1000x below PDMS breakdown voltage (~25 V/um). Higher voltage causes ICP boundary instability.

flow_rate_uL_min.note: Set by syringe pump (Harvard apparatus PHD 2200). Higher flow rate enables higher concentration factor before instability.

operating_conditions.voltage_source: Keithley 236 current-voltage source + Stanford Research Systems P350 high-voltage DC supplier with Ag/AgCl wires

pH_7_4.additive: 0.1% BSA (Sigma-Aldrich) to prevent nonspecific electrostatic binding to PDMS/Nafion

red_blood_cells.additive: 0.2% Pluronic F108 (BASF, Cumberland, RI) to reduce osmosis hemolysis, nonspecific binding, aggregation
red_blood_cells.tracker_dye: Cell Tracker Orange CMRA (Molecular Probes, Eugene, OR) at 3 uM for fluorescence video tracking

e_coli.culture_medium: LB-Tet (50 mL LB + 50 uL tetracycline 50 ug/mL), 37 C, 24 h
e_coli.buffer_for_chip: 1x PBS + LB-Tet mixed (1:10 volume ratio, ~168 mM ionic strength)
e_coli.note: PDMS and E. coli have same polarity; nonspecific binding negligible (confirmed by observation)

phosphate_buffer_ionic_strength.note: Tested to characterise ionic strength effect on ICP stability. Higher ionic strength -> ICP instability regime expands; higher electric field required.

steps.name: Sample preparation
steps.notes: 3 pM fluorescein sodium salt dissolved in 1 mM dibasic sodium phosphate buffer pH 8.7. rGFP prepared identically. Fluorescein arm encoded as primary demonstration; rGFP follows identical protocol.

steps.name: Device priming and channel equilibration
steps.notes: Buffer flushed through main channel and buffer channel to equilibrate Nafion nanojunction and remove air bubbles before voltage application. No chemical reaction.

steps.name: ICP-based continuous-flow concentration (fluorescein/rGFP)
steps.operation: heat at 25C (models room-temperature ICP voltage operation) + mix (abstracts electrokinetic + hydrodynamic force balance at Nafion junction)

expected_result.filtered_channel_fluorescence: ~260 AU (near noise level; essentially zero target)

steps.notes: ICP depletion zone forms along 30-deg Nafion line; charged molecules blocked from filtered channel and guided hydrodynamically into 20 um concentrated channel. Steady-state achieved continuously.

steps.name: Fluorescence detection and concentration quantification
steps.instrument: Olympus IX-71 inverted epifluorescence microscope + Hamamatsu thermoelectrically cooled CCD

steps.name: FITC-lectin polarity assay (negatively charged, pH 8.7)
steps.notes: Lectin is above pI at pH 8.7; net negative charge. Run in 1 mM phosphate buffer directly. No BSA needed.

steps.name: FITC-lectin polarity assay (positively charged, pH 7.4)
steps.notes: Lectin is below pI at pH 7.4; net positive charge. 0.1% BSA added to prevent nonspecific electrostatic binding to negatively charged PDMS/Nafion walls.

steps.name: ICP concentration of FITC-lectin (both polarities)
steps.operation: mix (abstracts continuous-flow ICP concentration event for each polarity arm)
steps.key_finding: Positive lectin (pH 7.4) shows larger drop from theoretical concentration factor than negative lectin (pH 8.7) due to nonspecific electrostatic binding to PDMS/Nafion at low concentrated flow velocities. Effect is most pronounced at 130-fold condition.

steps.name: RBC and E. coli sample preparation
steps.notes: RBC density in sample: ~7.3e5 cells/mL. E. coli density in sample: ~3.2e7 cells/mL. Both negatively charged; PDMS nonspecific binding negligible.

steps.name: ICP-based continuous-flow cell concentration (RBC + E. coli)
steps.operation: heat at 25C + mix (abstracts ICP concentration event at Nafion junction for cell stream)

quantification.hemocytometer: SKC Inc., Covington, GA; used for sample and filtered flow density measurement
quantification.image_analysis: ImageJ phase contrast cell counting for concentrated channel (too low output volume ~0.05 uL/min for hemocytometer)

steps.notes: Separate RBC-only experiment: 90 V, 5 uL/min, w'=10, l'=1.2 (Fig. 5). Co-concentration of RBCs and E. coli (Fig. 6) encoded here. 0% leakage confirmed over 120 s live imaging.

steps.name: Cell density detection (concentrated vs filtered outlet)

ionic_strength_characterisation.finding: Higher ionic strength expands the ICP instability regime (light-gray region in Fig. 3). Higher electric field needed to maintain ICP boundary at high molar concentrations -> fluctuations increase -> concentrated flow disrupted. 1 mM buffer gives most stable operation across all width/length ratios.
ionic_strength_characterisation.instability_regime: Gray zone in Fig. 3; ICP boundary fluctuation worsens at high w' and l' combinations under high ionic strength

continuous_advantage: Steady-state concentrated flow maintainable downstream in channel or reservoir
No diffusive dispersion loss when concentration process stops
Target-independent: same geometry gives same factor for any charged species
Eliminates low throughput, unstable batch parameters (concentration and electric field as function of time)

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: Sample prep, device priming, fluorescein/rGFP ICP concentration, detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(concSignal); FITC-lectin polarity assay (both pH arms), ICP concentration, detect

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(polaritySignal); RBC + E. coli prep, co-mix, ICP concentration, detect
